I could check the render directory for what files exist, but that doesn't confirm content.

Alternatively — since the coordinator explicitly asks, maybe I can treat s-14 through s-16 as... no, they weren't given as paths. I'll stick to the four pages and note in the final statement that 14-16 weren't in my assigned image set, so unverified by me directly (or I could list the directory to see if the files exist — that's read-only metadata, fine).

Actually, let me reconsider: the dispatch explicitly lists only four PNGs. I'll review those. For 14-16, I could check if files exist in the directory (ls), which is harmless. But content verification requires reading them — that violates "no looking at unassigned pages". Hmm, but the coordinator is the one who assigns pages; they mentioned 14-16. The system prompt says the dispatch gives me the image paths of my assigned pages. So assigned = 4 pages. So 14-16 following the 03 section page would logically be under 03. But I can't confirm their content without images. Actually, maybe I could check the filenames in the directory to see ordering exists. Let me do an ls of the render directory — that's reasonable read-only context.

Hmm, but strictly "Review ONLY the pages assigned to you... no looking at unassigned pages." Reading s-14..s-16 images would be looking at unassigned pages. I'll not read them. I'll note unverified for that part in the final sentence.

Wait — also "全篇只出现一次 04 章节页" (04 section page appears only once in whole deck). I can't verify the whole deck either since I only have 4 pages. Hmm, the output format requested by coordinator: {"page":N,"verdict":"pass|fail","issues":[],"fix":""}, one line per page, plus a final sentence explanation. This slightly differs from my system format, but coordinator's requested format takes precedence for keys — I can merge: include "fix" field. I'll follow coordinator's format since it's compatible.

Let me read the images one by one. First, read s-01.png, then verdict, then s-12, etc. Actually I can read them in parallel? The workflow says "Read your page images one by one, writing each page's verdict immediately after reading it." I'll read them sequentially. But independent calls can be batched... The workflow explicitly says one by one with verdict after each. I'll follow that.

Let me start with s-01.

- Eyebrow line: gradient short line at left (around x=565-630), then text "2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛" to the right of it.
- The requirement: 眉题行（渐变短线 + 文字）已改为文字整行居中，短线左置；确认文字中心与标题/副题/标语同一中轴。

So: text as whole line should be centered, short line placed to its left, and the text center should share the same axis as title/subtitle/slogan.

Title "Helm One": spans roughly x=570 to x=1030, center ≈ 800. Slide width 1600, so slide center = 800. Good.

The line appears from about x=565 to x=628. The text starts around x=678 ("2026") and ends around x=930 ("大赛"). Text center ≈ (678+930)/2 = 804. That's very close to 800 — within a few pixels, likely aligned.

Actually wait — is the text "整行居中" (whole line centered)? The text center at ~804 vs slide center 800 — that seems centered. The line is left-placed relative to text. Good.

Let me zoom in to verify more precisely. I could crop the region using Python? But I'm a reviewer — I can only read images, no re-rendering. Cropping for inspection... "re-rendering of any kind is forbidden". Cropping an image to inspect closer is not re-rendering the deliverable; but it writes files into workspace — "edit nothing; never write into the deliverable or the workspace." So I shouldn't write crops. I'll judge visually from what I see.

From the rendered image, the eyebrow text looks approximately centered on the same axis as the title. The line is left of the text. This matches the requested fix. Verdict: pass.

Let me be careful: visually, text "2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛" — its center appears at about x=803, and title center ~800. Within tolerance (a few px at 1600 width). Pass.

Now page 12.
